data.reasoning: The package is a standard AUR VCS package for a Rust-based Neovim plugin. The PKGBUILD clones from the official upstream GitHub repository (https://github.com/linw1995/nvim-mcp), uses standard cargo build commands (cargo fetch --locked, cargo build --frozen --release), and has no suspicious network activity or obfuscation. The install script is purely informational (heredoc with usage instructions). The .SRCINFO contains standard metadata. The deepseek model provided a thorough and accurate SAFE assessment with detailed reasoning about the build process and file contents.
data.disagreement_analysis: The apparent disagreement was caused by a tool error in the qwen model (HTTP 400 API failures for PKGBUILD and nvim-mcp-git.install), not by substantive security concerns. The deepseek model provided a thorough SAFE assessment with detailed reasoning. The openrouter/free model also assessed SAFE but is advisory-only and doesn't count as a vote per the rules.
coverage_issues: qwen model experienced API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) when reviewing PKGBUILD and nvim-mcp-git.install during full review, resulting in no verdict signal from that model despite producing an initial SAFE assessment for PKGBUILD
learnings: Tool reliability issues (API errors) can create apparent disagreements that are not substantive security concerns - the audit tool should distinguish between tool failures and actual security findings
Models correctly identified standard AUR patterns (VCS packages with SKIP checksums, standard build tool commands, informational install scripts) as safe and did not flag them as concerns
Advisory reports should be clearly distinguished from substantive votes in the final verdict calculation to avoid confusion about agreement levels
